activity_context.topic_title: The Vector Equation of a Plane

feedback.problem: Find an equation of the plane that contains the point $Q(3,2,2)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n=⟨2,2,3⟩.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, notice that the position vector of $Q$ is $q=⟨3,2,2⟩,$ $n=⟨2,2,3⟩$ is normal to the plane.

The equation of the plane that passes though the point $Q({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n$ can be given as

$$
(r-q)\cdot n=0,
$$

where $r$ is the position vector of any point on the plane, and $q$ is the position vector of $Q.$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-q)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-q\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =q\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨2,2,3⟩ & =⟨3,2,2⟩\cdot ⟨2,2,3⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨2,2,3⟩ & =16.\end{aligned}
$$
